Team — forwarding Horizon's redlines. Two immediate asks from procurement/legal: 1) confirm limits on InsightEdge (analytics subprocessor), 2) explicit exclusion of customer content from model training. They also request retention shortened from 90d.

Please see attached redline (Horizon_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) and their notes. Quick asks below — please reply with option and recommended wording so I can respond to Nora: 

- Security (Karthik): can we commit that InsightEdge will only receive aggregated, non-identifying telemetry and will have no access to request/response content? If yes, what guardrails (encryption, contract, SOC2) do we require?

- Product (Jordan): what is the product impact of not allowing training on customer content? Do we rely on customer content for model improvement or quality telemetry? Is there an alternative (obfuscated telemetry / sampled indices)?

Options to propose to customer (ranked preferred):
A) Allow InsightEdge for aggregated metrics only; contractually prohibit content access + SOC2 attestation + 30d telemetry retention for pilot; no training on customer content.
B) Deny InsightEdge access to any telemetry beyond operational metrics; retain 90d but redact identifiers; no training on content.
C) If we cannot accept training exclusion globally, offer a carveout: no training on customer prompts unless customer opts in and explicitly uploads data to a labeled training bucket.

Please respond by EOD so procurement doesn't stall. Thanks —

Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline + question on analytics subprocessor and training clause — security assessment

Olga / Jordan —

Security stance (summary): we can accept InsightEdge as a telemetry subprocessor under strict conditions:

- Data handed to InsightEdge must be pre-aggregated and tokenized; no customer prompt/response content may be forwarded.
- Contractual requirement: SOC 2 Type II attestation (or equivalent), written limitation of use to operational analytics, and right-to-audit clause limited to telemetry pipelines.
- Technical safeguards: TLS in transit, encryption at rest, short-lived retention policies (configurable), and access control with MFA and role-based restrictions.

On model training: we treat customer prompts/outputs as sensitive. We can commit to a default policy: "No training on customer prompt/response content without explicit customer opt-in." We already have a technical path to isolate and mark datasets for opt-in training buckets.

Retention: 90d is higher than our default for pilot customers. We can propose 30d for pilot, with the ability to extend to 90d upon customer approval or for operational troubleshooting with notice. That would be a reasonable commercial compromise.

Recommended customer-facing language (short):
"Redwood will not use customer prompt or response content to train models or improve model weights unless the customer explicitly opts in to a labeled training program. Where telemetry is shared with third-party analytics providers, Redwood will only share aggregated and de-identified metrics; such providers must hold a SOC 2 Type II attestation and are contractually prohibited from accessing customer prompt/response content."

If legal wants stronger right-to-audit language, we can add a narrow audit window limited to telemetry systems only.

Karthik
Head of Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline + question on analytics subprocessor and training clause — product impact

Olga / Karthik —

Product notes:

- We do not use raw customer prompts to train models by default in our hosted product. Most improvements come from internal eval datasets and opt-in customer programs. So committing to "no training without opt-in" is low-risk for us.
- Operational telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts, model variant usage) is valuable for runbook automation and incident triage; we can provide aggregated metrics only.
- If we accept a 30-day retention for pilot, we should instrument a support escalation path: keep a 90-day soft window accessible to SREs for incident investigation (notice to customer and logged access), but not routinely processed for analytics. That addresses both product troubleshooting and procurement concerns.

Recommended next steps for response to Horizon: accept Karthik's language, propose the 30d pilot retention with the 90d investigatory window (explicitly documented), and offer an opt-in checkbox for training if they later want to participate.

Happy to draft a short clause for procurement if you want me to.

Jordan Blake
SVP, Product
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA redline + question on analytics subprocessor and training clause — Redwood proposed language

Nora —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We reviewed this with Product and Security. Below is Redwood's proposed compromise language and next steps so procurement can move forward: 

Proposed contractual language (to insert into section X.Y):
"Redwood will not use customer prompt or response content to train models or improve model weights unless the customer explicitly opts in to a labeled training program. Where telemetry is shared with third-party analytics providers, Redwood will only share metrics that have been aggregated and de-identified such that they cannot be reasonably re-associated with an individual customer request. Third-party analytics providers must maintain SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent) attestation and shall be contractually prohibited from accessing raw customer prompt or response content. Redwood will provide a limited right to audit telemetry pipelines related to such providers, restricted to the scope necessary to confirm non-access to customer content."

Telemetry retention for pilot: we can accept a 30-day rolling retention for operational telemetry during the pilot phase. For serious incident investigation that requires deeper historical context, Redwood may access a 90-day investigatory window only when triggered by an active support ticket; such access will be logged and Redwood will provide notice to the customer.

If Horizon agrees to the above, we will:
- Replace the corresponding redline text in Horizon_DPA_redline_v3.pdf and re-send a clean DPA for signature.
- Provide InsightEdge's SOC 2 summary and a description of the telemetry fields shared (we will redact any identifiers).

Please let me know if the proposed language addresses your team's concerns or if you want a short call to finalize. If acceptable, procurement can proceed to countersignature and we'll route InsightEdge docs to your legal contact.

Thanks —

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
